body: Dr. Avery Chen already sends tissue to Tempus. Last visit they asked about adding liquid at progression rather than waiting on a new biopsy.
Dr. Jordan Chen is still on FMI for most solid-tumor orders. They want a clearer story for HER2-low therapy decisions before considering a switch.
Dr. Riley Chen asked whether HRD status is confirmed before later-line therapy. They are also tracking gyn academic trial eligibility.
Dr. Quinn Chen is concerned about turnaround time versus Guardant liquid. They remain interested in a thoracic liquid option if we can address that concern.
Dr. Morgan Chen prefers the in-house lab for surgical gyn specimens. They are open to a send-out conversation if specimen flow stays simple.
Dr. Casey Chen is unsure which lab they use for heme. They asked which tumor-only panel path to order so heme cases do not follow the solid-tumor plus-normal workflow.
Dr. Harper Chen already orders a lot of Tempus. Last visit they wanted better operational follow-through on pending cases rather than a new assay pitch.
Dr. Drew Chen still uses FMI at the independent practice. They asked how community gyn clinics get HRD findings without a long send-out.
